tables.name: users
tables.purpose: Stores application users so that each task can be owned by exactly one user and users can only access their own tasks.

columns.name: password_hash
columns.notes: Hashed password (e.g. bcrypt/argon2); never store plain text

columns.name: display_name
columns.notes: Optional name shown in the UI

columns.name: updated_at
columns.notes: Last update time (UTC); maintained by application or trigger

tables.name: tasks
tables.purpose: Stores tasks created by users, including title, optional description and completion status (supports create, complete/uncomplete, delete, and list/filter features).

columns.name: user_id
columns.notes: FK to users.id; ON DELETE CASCADE so removing a user removes their tasks

columns.name: title
columns.notes: Required; must be non-empty after trimming (enforce with CHECK (length(btrim(title)) > 0) and API validation)

columns.name: is_completed
columns.notes: Completion status; new tasks start incomplete; can be toggled back to false

columns.name: completed_at
columns.notes: Set when marked complete; set to NULL when unmarked

columns.name: created_at
columns.notes: Creation time (UTC); used for default list ordering

relationships.notes: Each task belongs to exactly one user; ON DELETE CASCADE. Inverse side (one user owns many tasks) is represented by this relationship.

assumptions: PostgreSQL is the target database, so gen_random_uuid() (pgcrypto or PostgreSQL 13+) is used for uuid primary keys.
The single role 'User' is represented by the users table; no roles table is needed because there is only one role.
Every task belongs to exactly one user, satisfying the requirement that users can only access their own tasks; the API must filter all queries by the authenticated user_id.
The one-to-many relationship between users and tasks is modeled only once, on the tasks table via the user_id foreign key, since the FK column resides in tasks.
No many-to-many relationships exist in the requirements, so no junction tables are required.
Deletion is permanent (hard delete) as per F3, so no soft-delete column (deleted_at) is included.
Task status is modeled as a boolean is_completed (complete/incomplete only), with completed_at as an optional timestamp for when it was completed.
Task titles are required and non-empty; a CHECK constraint and application validation enforce this. Description is optional (nullable).
Authentication uses email and password hash; session/token storage is handled outside the database (e.g. stateless JWT) and is not modeled.
All timestamps are stored in UTC; updated_at is maintained by the application or a database trigger.
The composite indexes on tasks (user_id, is_completed) and (user_id, created_at) support filtering by status and ordered list views within the 2-second performance target.
